newsitem.title: UK: Dying hurricane lashes Europe, at least five die.
newsitem.headline: Dying hurricane lashes Europe, at least five die.

text.p: A dying hurricane lashed parts of northern Europe during the night, felling trees, disrupting ferry and rail services and flooding coastal areas, police and emergency workers said on Tuesday.
At least five people were killed in road accidents when trees collapsed or big waves swept over coastal defences.

Gales and heavy rain pummeled Britain overnight, blocking roads and leaving thousands of homes without power. It was the worst storm to hit Britain since October, 1987, when a hurricane destroyed 15 million trees and caused hundreds of millions of dollars worth of damage.
British meteorologists blamed spin-offs from Hurricane Lili, which caused widespread damage in Cuba and the Bahamas just over a week ago before finally veering eastwards over the Atlantic.
"While it lasted, it was a wild night," a spokesman for the London Weather Centre said.
By Tuesday morning the storms had cleared but the effects continued. Rail services were badly disrupted in Britain and the Netherlands.
Many ferry services connecting Britain and France and Britain and Ireland were cancelled or delayed. Dutch ferry services were also affected.

Passengers and crew endured a nightmare channel crossing when their ferry, P&O's Pride of Calais, was battered by 10-metre (35-foot) waves and took 10 hours longer than normal to make the 75-minute Calais to Dover crossing.
In France, a 15-year-old cyclist was swept from a seaside path by a wave and presumed drowned near the Channel port of Saint Malo, police said.

On Britain's south coast, where winds gusted at up to 90 miles (145 km) an hour, numerous vessels broke from their moorings, coastguards said. In Minehead on the Bristol Channel in western England, huge chunks of concrete were ripped from the sea defences.
A North Sea oil rig platform with 69 people on board drifted from its moorings off the coast of Scotland but was safely reconnected to a tow line.
One elderly man was killed and a woman injured in road accidents in northern England and a British couple were killed when a tree hit their car but their three-year-old son survived.
The Irish meteorological service said winds of 80 miles (130 km) an hour were recorded on the west coast of Ireland. Two people died in a car crash in Carlow in the southeast.

In the low-lying Netherlands, water and shipping authorities started intensive monitoring of dikes in the southwestern province of Zeeland. Authorities predicted seas would reach 3.70 metres (12 feet), a phenomenon which normally does not occur more than every five years.
